title: Functions
description: Package reusable application logic behind named boundaries with formal parameters, explicit return values, and clear caller contracts.

objectives.statement: Declare and invoke JavaScript functions that accept parameters and return computed results to the caller.
Distinguish return values from console.log side-effects to ensure callers receive computable values.
Compose multiple small, single-responsibility functions to process multi-stage calculations.

content.title: Packaging Logic Behind Reusable Names
content.hook: Without functions, every calculation must be re-typed wherever it is needed.
content.context: Functions allow you to wrap a block of code, give it a meaningful name, accept variable inputs as parameters, and return a computed result. They create predictable boundaries that keep programs organized, testable, and maintainable.
goals: Understand how functions package reusable logic behind clear parameters.
Distinguish return values from console.log side effects.
Capture function call return values into variables for downstream processing.

content.title: The Function Boundary: Inputs, Execution, and Outputs
content.description: Visual diagram illustrating the execution boundary: Calling code passes arguments (100, 0.08) into parameter bindings (price, taxRate). The body calculates and executes return price + (price * taxRate). The return keyword substitutes the call expression with 108, assigning it to const total.

printMultiply calls console.log but does NOT return anything. In JavaScript, a function with no return statement returns undefined.

feedback.correct: Spot on! console.log prints to standard output and returns undefined. The return statement is required to hand computed values back to the calling code.
feedback.incorrect: console.log is purely a display side-effect. To give a caller data to work with, a function must use the return statement.

hints.content: console.log displays information to developers, but only return passes data back to code.

content.question: Why does assigning the result of a function that only uses console.log store undefined in a variable?

options.text: console.log is an output side-effect that prints to the console; it evaluates to undefined rather than returning a value to the caller.
console.log can only output text to the browser window and cannot communicate with variables.
Variables declared with const refuse to store output from built-in browser functions.
JavaScript functions automatically delete any returned values if console.log was invoked inside them.

content.title: Functions Takeaway
takeaways: Functions package reusable logic behind clear input parameters and return contracts.
return delivers data to the caller; console.log only displays text for inspection.
Functions allow complex systems to be built from small, testable, single-responsibility units.
